text:
maria: Heads-up — after the remap/compact change from last week I'm seeing steady GPU memory growth on long-context paged-attn runs (RTX6000). repro is small but consistent.

devin: Which remap change? commit id? diff? :eyes:

maria: commit 8f3b2a1 (kvcache: aggressive slab remap on free). repro steps below. attaching short logs.

sachin: Is this the fragmentation or stale-owner variant? last time we saw aliasing it was a stale-owner write during eviction.

maria: Not exactly stale-owner write. I think it's a remap-induced alias: two different slab IDs end up pointing to same phys page after concurrent coalesce + remap. Happens under sustained longctx growth + batch=1 streaming.

alyssa: Can you paste the minimal repro command? I'll try on MI250X tonight.

maria: ./run_longctx_repro --model=gptx-8k --batch=1 --seq=16000 --enable-paging --repro-seed=42

maria: log snippet:
```
2026-03-17T12:03:45Z kvcache: remap slab id=42 -> slot=7 (from gpu0)
2026-03-17T12:03:45Z kvcache: remap slab id=99 -> slot=7 (from gpu1)
2026-03-17T12:03:45Z page_table: alias detected: phys=0x7ffab3c000 mapped by gpu0,gpu1
2026-03-17T12:03:45Z kvcache: alloc_fail: slab_coalesce failed, fallback to spare_arena
2026-03-17T12:03:50Z runtime: pagefault storm, kv-evict thrash -> memory growth
```

jordan: That alias line is the smoking gun. We have atomicity gap in remap+install where two GPUs can race and win the same slot. Could be ordering inversion on PCIe events.

devin: On RTX family we saw intermittent PCI ordering differences vs NVLink. MI250X might show the same but with different timings. @sachin any hardware-specific ideas?

sachin: MI250X DMA coalescing can reorder completions; if our install path assumes completion ordering we're toast. We should add an ownership stamp (shadow-stamp) on the PT entry and check on install.

alyssa: Quick mitigation: disable aggressive remap (fall back to append-only slab) and increase prefix-cache to avoid early coalesces. That stops the growth on my local CI.

infra-bot: deploy-canary started for kvcache-hotfix/disable-remap (build b214).

maria: Canary deployed to 3 hosts (RTX6000). After 10min the leak stops. Growth curve flattens.

devin: Can you paste perf sample (top lines) from the repro run so we can see hot paths?

maria: perf top:
```
kvcache_coalesce                    42.1%
kvcache_remap_install               21.6%
page_table_install                 12.3%
kernel_paged_attn_dispatch         8.9%
memcpy_async                       5.4%
```

jordan: So majority time in coalesce+remap path. We should be able to add a cheap ownership check before remap_install to avoid aliasing.

sachin: I'll prototype shadow-stamp (64-bit epoch + slab-id) and make install atomic with compare-exchange on the PT slot. If CAS fails we rollback. That should be cross-arch safe.

alyssa: Also add a fuzz test that interleaves remap/coalesce with artificial DMA-completion reordering. Found a micro-repro by delaying completion callbacks by 0..10ms.

maria: Filing bug with traces + repro package. Patch PR in progress: https://git.internal/repro/REDW-kt/422 (WIP).

devin: Good. After PR we should run the repro across RTX6000, A100, MI250X, H100. Make an ops runbook to toggle remap flag per-queue.

maria: Agreed. For now canary disable + shadow-stamp PR. Will update when CI passes on MI250X. :thumbsup:

jordan: Nice detective work. add regression test to nightly perf harness so we catch this on future remap changes. :bug: :eyes:
